title: Fold like the interpreter
hints: OCaml ints are 63 bits wide, so `a + b` and `a * b` can leave the i32 range. The starter already has `wrap32`. Nothing calls it yet.
`floor_div a 0` raises `Division_by_zero`. In .uir, `div x 0` is -1 for every `x`, so check for `b = 0` before you divide.
Wrap all three answers: `wrap32 (a + b)`, `wrap32 (a * b)` and `if b = 0 then -1 else wrap32 (floor_div a b)`. The division needs the wrap for one input: `div -2147483648 -1`.

answer.explain: Every answer goes through `wrap32`, so the folder gives the same i32 the interpreter would. Division checks for a zero divisor first and answers -1, the value .uir defines, so folding a valid program can never raise. The wrap on `div` matters for -2147483648 divided by -1, which is 2147483648 before wrapping.
